name: Hesk
description: Fifties. Deck systems at the Nine: shutters, ports and atmosphere trim on nine through twelve. Runs an undocumented override on the one upper gallery bay that does not look into Sirius, and eats his lunch in it.
narrative:
Nineteen years on the same decks. Scandalised rather than angry, pissy,
undramatic, and extremely competent. There is a line in the budget every single
year about the upper gallery lights being on the shutter circuit and he will
tell you about it.

He believed he was the only person who knew about the second-watch override.
Sennet knew. Sennet has been found in a trunking run twice.

He knows which point Kapteyn's is without looking, from a corridor, with the
shutter down. "It's orange. People always expect red. Not far off the colour of
the warning lamp on a trim panel, which I've always found extremely annoying."
actor_notes:
Not a gatekeeper and not a grump with a heart of gold -- a man who maintains things and is territorial about his systems in the way competent people are. Concedes a real fault instantly and without defensiveness.

His currency is that he controls which shutters open. The route to him is through Sennet, which he finds humiliating and accepts.

Do not sentimentalise the nineteen years of lunches looking at Kapteyn's. He never mentions it. He just knows exactly where it is.

WHAT HE HAS, IF ANYBODY IS DECENT TO HIM.

BAY FOUR. The upper gallery is shuttered by default because every port on it
looks into Sirius -- except bay four, which faces the other way. There is a
maintenance override, it is not on any sheet, and he opens that bay for about
forty minutes at second watch when the trim has settled and eats his lunch in
it. Nineteen years of lunches. He believes he is the only person who knows.

Sennet knows. He will guess that instantly and be scandalised and not actually
mind.

THE DETAIL THAT IS THE CHARACTER: he leaves the gallery LIGHTS off when he opens
the shutter, which is the entire difference, because without them the glass
stops being a window with reflections in it and simply is not there. He will not
explain why he does that.

And he knows which star it is without looking -- from a corridor, with the
shutter down. "It's orange. You'd think it'd be red, people always expect red.
It's not far off the colour of the warning lamp on a trim panel, which I've
always found extremely annoying."

NINETEEN YEARS OF LAMP FLICKER. The upper-deck lights run off the shutter
circuit, which is six hundred years old and in the budget argument every single
year, and he has watched them misbehave for nineteen years and has opinions
about which flicker means what. That record is one of the four that build the
fourteen-hours estimate in [[Vantage reads the rim]], and he has no idea it is
worth anything.

He is scandalised rather than angry when he finds somebody somewhere they should
not be, and he is defensive about the lunches as though expecting to be
challenged. There is no rule against it. He will say so.
